text:
Recent work supports treating elapsed time as information beyond event position. [E-NSDE (NeurIPS 2024)](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/7cdbd53dfbcf9a5263227555aac5b9cd-Abstract-Conference.html) models continuous interest evolution and links interaction gaps to predictive uncertainty; it does not establish that older events should always receive less weight. [TiM4Rec (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neucom.2025.131270) integrates time awareness into a state-space backbone, useful motivation but outside the required BERT4Rec family. A directly relevant [2026 BERT4Rec study](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44163-026-01554-z) combines content relevance with continuous time decay and jointly learned session gating. Its reported results motivate temporal adaptation, but do not establish gains under this benchmark’s splits or candidate sampling.

Feasible adaptation, inferred from these mechanisms: retain one bidirectional masked-item network and introduce learned per-head biases for bucketed pairwise timestamp gaps, following the interval principle of [TiSASRec](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf). Optionally condition a nonnegative decay rate on observed history so content attention can preserve useful older interactions. For appended-MASK inference, anchor its timestamp to the last observed interaction; use the same history-only convention for terminal-mask training. This measures historical age, not the unknown wait until the next event. Compare against the established cutoff control and a position-only model, with matched training budgets; shuffled-gap ablation can test whether actual timestamps help. Select by macro validation HR@10 across all four categories. Healthy margins and concentrated representations alone cannot identify intent drift as the failure cause.
